maya: Heads-up: int4 canary (fenrir-liteq) producing invalid JSON on structured-output tests; parser complains with 'Control character' errors.
sam: Seeing same. Only on streaming responses and when emojis or non-ascii punctuation present. Fails ~0.8% in canary vs 0.01% baseline.
henry: Thanks — can you paste a minimal example?
maya: Minimal chunk that reproduces locally:```json
{"action": "create_ticket", "meta": "subject:​Missing owner — please review"}
``` Parser error: `JSONDecodeError: Invalid control character at: line 1 column 45 (char 44)`
sam: Our logs show the offending byte as 0xE2 at the start of a 3-byte sequence; looks like a stray ZWSP/U+200B encoded as 0xE2 0x80 0x8B split across stream boundaries.
li: Could be tokenizer/chunk boundary interplay. Quantized int4 sampling seems to increase chances of breaking multi-byte sequences.
ops-bot: Canary run stats: 2k calls, parse_fail=16, streaming_only=true, quant_mode=int4.
henry: Hypothesis: streaming chunk boundary split + quant noise -> broken UTF-8 sequence -> parser sees control char / replacement -> json lib errors. Two-pronged fix: (1) make parser pre-buffer and repair UTF-8 at chunk stitch, (2) conservative sanitizer to remove ZWSP & C0 controls before parsing.
maya: We should avoid overzealous stripping because emojis are valid. Proposal: strip U+200B (ZWSP) and the C0 range except for \n and \t. Pseudocode:```python
def repair(s):
    s = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', s)
    s = re.sub(r"[\u0000-\u001F&&[^\n\t]]", "", s)
    s = s.replace('\u200b', '')
    return s
```
sam: Also add chunk-level utf8 repair when assembling streaming pieces: `buf = (buf + chunk).encode('utf-8', 'replace').decode('utf-8')` before parsing payload. That fixes broken multi-byte codepoints.
henry: Telemetry: capture `repr(first_8_bytes)` and `len(chunk)` and `quant_seed` when parse fails. Also capture token ids around boundary to triage tokenizer correlation.
li: I'll add token id dump to canary harness and correlate with tokenizer split heuristics.
maya: Short-term mitigation in runtime: if structured parse fails -> retry once with non-streaming call + repair, and if success, continue; if still fails, return soft fallback and avoid re-invoking external tool (use idempotency token).
sam: Important: ensure retry budget and dedupe header so we don't double-create resources on tool invoke. Add `X-Redwood-Tool-Idempotency: <uid>` to tool calls.
henry: Tests: add unit `test_nonascii_stream_parse_repair` and a canary that injects ZWSP and emojis into prompt to reproduce. Nightly canary should monitor delta vs baseline.
maya: I'll open a PR with sanitizer + streaming repair + test. Will add metric tag `quant_mode=int4` to parse_fail counter.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary-sanitizer v0.32 -> staging tonight (ETA 02:00 UTC).
sam: Thanks — after PR lands, please run targeted canary with 50k streaming calls to validate fix under load.
henry: Also run tokenization delta between fp16 and int4 on the same prompts to confirm quant increases boundary splits.
maya: Action items: (1) PR sanitizer + tests (maya), (2) add token id telemetry to canary (li), (3) dedupe/idempotency header in toolchain (sam), (4) night canary + 50k run and report (henry).
maya: assigning and will update thread. :thumbsup:
